terminology.details: I understand the version as the specified edition and SHA-256 as a deterministic fingerprint of exact bytes. The b prefix denotes bytes; the model parameters are stored learned numbers. LoRA is the optional small correction used with its base, while ASR first transcribes speech for the same chat core. A token is a generated text unit that need not equal a Chinese character, so 384 new tokens is a generation budget. CER is character edit count divided by source-transcript characters. The NFKC paragraph provides a usable character-form example (fullwidth to halfwidth digits), and the revised OCR row directly states normalization, complete whitespace removal, preservation of script differences and normalized punctuation. FLEURS/AISHELL function as named sources whose roles/counts are supplied here. On this reread I found no remaining undefined term that blocks the stated interpretation or exercise.

program_explanation.details: There is one current target Python fence and no target shell command. It imports sha256, defines artificial expected and received bytes, prints hexadecimal fingerprints shortened to 12 characters using hexdigest()[:12], then compares the complete binary digests via digest(). The printed abbreviation does not weaken the actual comparison in this example; real downloads still require complete fingerprints and size. I exact-byte-compared the entire current fence to my previously executed script. The earlier original output was 45de0d2401bf, b43173684456 and False, while the exercise received = expected variant output was 45de0d2401bf twice and True. I reuse those genuine results, with no rerun claim. The programs hash handwritten text, not model files, and neither output assesses answer quality.

exercise.details: My current prediction is still False for the differing byte strings and True after assigning received = expected; the unchanged-fence comparison makes my earlier own execution applicable. The card tests read-aloud speech and does not validate noisy conversational use. These are future test designs, not measured answers. formula_and_number_understanding.CER: (insertions + deletions + substitutions) / source-transcript character count. Raw and normalized conventions can change both edit counts and reference lengths. Raw keeps spacing/punctuation; the stated normalized convention uses NFKC then whitespace removal and retains normalized punctuation/case/script differences.
formula_and_number_understanding.model_counts: 2,127,532,032 parameters identify the visual-language base; 808,878,080 identify the separate speech recognizer. Recognizer results are not LoRA improvement, and the selected release does not enable LoRA.
formula_and_number_understanding.generated_answers: 42+84+18+10+3+13+4+4 = 178 generated answers; 171 normally ended + 7 truncated = 178. The ASR row separately measures transcription character errors. The seven 384-new-token truncations belong to chat and remain in its 13-task denominator.
formula_and_number_understanding.pass_and_scope: Pass requires prior content criteria, following the request and normal ending. Shared images and voice questions limit independence; the source also distinguishes this course’s held-out test from possible upstream pretraining exposure. These counts are not a universal reliability guarantee or minimum-hardware measurement.
